newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: SOCCER-SPORTING BEAT PORTO TO NARROW GAP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SPORTING BEAT PORTO TO NARROW GAP.

text.p: Sporting beat Portuguese reigning champions Porto 2-1 on Saturday to turn up the heat in the race for this year's title with just 11 games to go before the end of the season.
It was the first time in 21 years that Sporting had beaten Porto at the champions' home stadium.

Porto, who have not won any of their last three games, are still in the lead with 57 points but Sporting have crept up to 50 points. Benfica, who meet Salgueiros at home on Sunday, are trailing with 43.

Porto, who play Manchester United in Portugal on Wednesday in the quarter-finals second round of the European Cup, have suffered from fatigue and faltering morale since the English side crushed them 4-0 in the first leg earlier this month.
Sporting opened the scoring in the 29th minute when defender Roberto Beto slipped the ball past the right post after an unchallenged cross from Pedro Barbosa.
Sporting, who have been chasing the league title for 14 years, extended their lead eight minutes into the second half when striker Pedro Barbosa, unmarked inside the box, hit home a header.
Porto's Jose Barroso scored his side's consolation goal in the 70th minute from a 25-metre free-kick which was so powerful that Belgian keeper De Wilde was forced to let it slip through his hands.
De Wilde compensated for this mistake with a spectacular save six minutes later to deny Brazilian striker Mario Jardel Porto's second goal.
"Sporting made use of their two opportunities to score while we didn't follow through on our chances of equalising which might have allowed us to actually win," said Porto coach Antonio Oliveira.
